Depending on how it's configured, a scale set's instances can be spread across fault domains within one datacenter, or across multiple availability zones.
eg: Combining autoscaling with either of those resiliency layouts means a scale set can absorb both a traffic spike and a rack- or zone-level failure without any manual intervention.

def: Extends Azure management — Azure Policy, RBAC, Azure Monitor, and tagging — to servers, Kubernetes clusters, and other infrastructure running outside Azure entirely: on-premises, at the edge, or in another cloud, by projecting each one as an Azure resource without migrating the underlying workload itself.
eg: A requirement to apply the same governance and monitoring tooling to on-premises servers that an organization already applies to its native Azure VMs, without actually moving those servers into Azure, is the signal for Azure Arc rather than a migration tool like Azure Migrate.

term: Azure Private Link service vs. private endpoint
def: A private endpoint is how a consumer privately reaches an existing PaaS resource. Azure Private Link service is the other side of that same mechanism: it lets an organization publish its own service, running behind a Standard Load Balancer, so that other VNets, or even other tenants, can connect to it through a private endpoint of their own, without that traffic ever crossing the public internet.
eg: A scenario about privately consuming someone else's PaaS resource needs a private endpoint; a scenario about an organization privately exposing its own custom service to outside consumers needs Private Link service on the provider's side.

term: API Management network integration: external vs. internal VNet modes
def: In external mode, Azure API Management's gateway, developer portal, and management endpoints get a public IP, while the backends it calls can still sit privately inside a VNet. In internal mode, every one of those endpoints, including the gateway itself, only gets a private IP inside the VNet, so APIs are reachable only from within that network or something connected to it, with no public endpoint existing at all.
eg: A requirement that an API only ever be reachable from inside the corporate network or over ExpressRoute, never from the public internet, is the signal for internal VNet mode specifically, not just locking down the backend behind the gateway.

term: Load Balancer SKUs: Basic vs. Standard
def: The Basic SKU was retired on 30 September 2025 (new deployments were blocked after 31 March 2025), so Standard is the only SKU to design with. Basic had no SLA, no zone redundancy, no outbound rules of its own, and was open by default, allowing inbound traffic even with no NSG attached. The Standard SKU adds a 99.99% SLA, supports a zone-redundant frontend IP, provides explicit outbound rules to manage SNAT port allocation, and is secure by default, blocking all inbound traffic unless an NSG explicitly allows it.
eg: That last difference catches teams off guard when upgrading an existing Basic load balancer to Standard: VMs that were reachable with no NSG at all under Basic suddenly become unreachable under Standard until an explicit allow rule is added, since Standard assumes nothing is allowed until an NSG says otherwise.

def: A global Layer 7 entry point for web applications. It routes HTTP(S) traffic over Microsoft's edge network to the closest healthy origin, and adds edge caching, TLS offload, Web Application Firewall protection, and health-probe-based failover in the data path.
eg: It is the pick for a multi-region web app that needs latency-based routing, fast failover, and one central WAF policy. Traffic Manager is DNS-only, and Application Gateway is regional.

def: A Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) load balancer that distributes inbound flows across healthy backend instances using a five-tuple hash and health probes. Public load balancers front internet traffic and internal ones front private traffic; the Standard SKU supports availability zones.
eg: It is regional and does not inspect HTTP, so path-based routing or a WAF needs Application Gateway or Front Door. For non-HTTP protocols or database tiers it is the usual choice.

def: A service that inspects incoming HTTP(S) requests and blocks common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting, using managed rule sets plus custom rules. In Azure it runs on Application Gateway and on Front Door.
eg: Stopping OWASP-style attacks centrally at the edge points to WAF on Front Door; a regional app behind Application Gateway uses WAF on that gateway. A network security group cannot detect these attacks.

def: A network of edge servers that caches static content close to users to cut latency and offload the origin. A cached file stays at the edge until its time to live expires (seven days by default if the origin sets none).
eg: Azure CDN from Microsoft (classic) retires on 30 September 2027, with Azure Front Door Standard and Premium as the successor, so new designs needing dynamic acceleration or WAF usually pick Front Door.

def: Managed Kubernetes: Azure operates the Kubernetes control plane while you choose and manage the worker node pools, scaling, and upgrades that run your containerized workloads.
eg: Choose AKS when you need full Kubernetes control, such as custom schedulers, operators, or a service mesh. If the team does not want to run a cluster, Container Apps is the lighter option.

def: A serverless platform for running containers and microservices without managing a cluster. It provides HTTP and event-driven autoscaling through KEDA, scale to zero, Dapr integration, and revisions for traffic splitting.
eg: It is the answer when a team wants container autoscaling, including scale to zero, with no node pools or cluster upgrades. AKS with KEDA can scale similarly but leaves cluster ownership with the team.

def: An open-source component that scales workloads based on event sources such as queue length or message backlog, including down to zero. It is built into Azure Container Apps and is available as an add-on for AKS.
eg: When a question pairs event-driven scaling with 'no cluster to manage', that points to Container Apps. With AKS you enable the KEDA add-on but still own node pools and upgrades.

def: Event-driven serverless compute that runs code in response to triggers such as HTTP requests, queue messages, or timers. Hosting plans include Flex Consumption (scales to zero, supports VNet integration), Premium (pre-warmed instances), Dedicated (an App Service plan), and the older Consumption plan.
eg: A short, event-triggered task with unpredictable volume fits Functions. Durable Functions add code-based orchestration, while Logic Apps suit low-code workflows with prebuilt connectors.

def: The set of compute resources (region, VM size, instance count, pricing tier) that one or more App Service apps run on. Every app in a plan shares its instances, so you scale the plan up or out rather than the individual app.
eg: Several apps in one plan save money but compete for the same CPU and memory, so a heavy app may need its own plan. Deployment slots require the Standard tier or higher.

def: Source network address translation rewrites a VM's private IP to a public IP for outbound internet connections, using a limited pool of ports per backend instance. When an instance runs out of allocated SNAT ports, new outbound connections to the same destination fail.
prompt: Source network address translation rewrites a VM's private IP to a public IP for outbound internet connections, using a limited pool of ports per backend instance. When an instance runs out of allocated _____ ports, new outbound connections to the same destination fail.
eg: Intermittent outbound failures under high connection volume are the symptom. The best fix is a NAT gateway on the subnet; extra public IPs or explicit outbound rules are lesser options.

def: The top SKU of the managed Azure network firewall, above Standard and Basic, adds TLS inspection, a signature-based intrusion detection and prevention system (IDPS), URL filtering that considers the full path, and web categories. It targets sensitive or regulated workloads that must inspect encrypted traffic.
eg: Standard filters on FQDNs, network rules, and threat intelligence but cannot look inside encrypted payloads. A requirement for TLS decryption plus IDPS in the hub means Premium.

def: An ExpressRoute add-on that links two ExpressRoute circuits so on-premises sites can exchange traffic with each other over the Microsoft global network instead of the public internet.
eg: It connects on-premises to on-premises; it does not add a backup path into Azure, so resilience needs a second circuit or a VPN failover. Linking across geopolitical regions requires Premium SKU circuits.

def: Microsoft's hybrid infrastructure solution that runs Azure-managed virtual machines, containers, and storage on validated hardware in your own datacenter or edge sites, connected to Azure through Azure Arc. It is the renamed Azure Stack HCI.
eg: A question that still says 'Azure Stack HCI' means the same product. It fits workloads that must stay on-premises for latency, data residency, or limited-connectivity reasons while using Azure management.

def: Custom entries in a route table associated with a subnet that override Azure's default system routes. Each route has an address prefix and a next hop (such as a virtual appliance, a virtual network gateway, or None to drop traffic), and the longest matching prefix wins.
eg: In hub-and-spoke, a 0.0.0.0/0 route whose next hop is the hub firewall's private IP forces spoke traffic through the firewall. Peering alone never sends traffic through an inspection device.

def: Lets you group VMs by role, such as web, app, or database, and use the group as the source or destination in network security group rules instead of IP addresses, so rules follow the workload as VMs are added or replaced.
eg: A rule like 'allow the web group to the app group on port 8080' stays valid as IPs change. All network interfaces in one group must be in the same virtual network.

term: Azure Batch and CycleCloud for batch and HPC compute
def: Azure Batch is a managed service for running large-scale parallel and high-performance computing jobs: you define pools of compute nodes, jobs, and tasks, and Batch schedules the tasks, scales the pool, and can use Spot VMs to cut cost. There is no charge for Batch itself, only for the underlying resources. Azure CycleCloud orchestrates traditional HPC clusters with schedulers such as Slurm.
eg: Embarrassingly parallel work such as rendering, simulations, or nightly processing of many files points to Batch. A scheduler-based cluster that scientists already know points to CycleCloud.

term: Choosing a VM-based solution: pricing and placement options
def: Spot VMs use spare capacity at a deep discount but can be evicted, so they suit interruptible work. Reservations and savings plans lower the cost of steady usage for one or three years. Azure Dedicated Host gives single-tenant physical servers for compliance or per-core licensing. Azure Compute Gallery shares versioned images across regions and subscriptions. Proximity placement groups keep VMs physically close for low latency.
eg: Interruptible means Spot, steady and predictable means reservations, and a physical-server isolation or licensing requirement means Dedicated Host.

def: Confidential computing protects data in use by running workloads in a hardware-based trusted execution environment, so that even the host and cloud operators cannot read memory. Confidential VMs offer this for lift-and-shift of whole VMs on hardware such as AMD SEV-SNP or Intel TDX, and keys can be released only to an attested workload using secure key release with Managed HSM.
eg: Encryption at rest and in transit are already standard. 'Protect data while it is being processed' is the signal for confidential computing.

def: A first-party Azure service that runs a VMware vSphere, vSAN, and NSX private cloud on dedicated bare-metal hosts in Azure. Workloads can move without conversion or re-IP using the same VMware tools, which suits datacenter exits on a deadline or applications that cannot be re-platformed, while Azure services can be added around it.
eg: A fast datacenter exit that keeps VMware skills and tooling points to Azure VMware Solution rather than rehosting each VM as a native Azure VM.

def: A single-tenant deployment of App Service that is injected into your virtual network and uses the Isolated v2 pricing tiers, giving network isolation, dedicated compute, and very high scale. It suits applications with strict isolation, compliance, or private-only requirements, at higher cost than the multitenant service.
eg: A web workload that must run in a dedicated, VNet-injected environment points to an App Service Environment. Regional VNet integration only covers outbound calls.

term: Azure Static Web Apps and Logic Apps hosting options
def: Azure Static Web Apps hosts static front ends and builds them from a GitHub or Azure DevOps repository, with globally distributed content and serverless API back ends. Logic Apps comes as Consumption (multitenant, pay per execution) or Standard (single-tenant runtime with multiple workflows per app, virtual network integration, and local development).
eg: A requirement for private networking or predictable pricing for many workflows points to Logic Apps Standard. Occasional, low-volume workflows suit Consumption.

term: Service Bus queues vs. Storage queues
def: Storage queues are simple and cheap, suit queues that stay below 80 GB, and are used with the standard Storage SDKs. Service Bus is chosen for guaranteed first-in-first-out ordering with sessions, automatic duplicate detection, dead-letter queues, transactions, topics and subscriptions for publish and subscribe, AMQP 1.0, and, in the Premium tier, messages up to 100 MB.
eg: A queue that needs ordering, duplicate detection, or a dead-letter queue is Service Bus. A simple work queue of small messages is a Storage queue.

term: Event Hubs and Event Grid design features
def: Event Hubs ingests streams through partitions that consumer groups read independently, can capture events automatically to Blob Storage or Data Lake Storage, and exposes a Kafka-compatible endpoint. Event Grid routes discrete events to handlers with filtering, retries, and dead-lettering, supports the MQTT and HTTP protocols, and offers system topics for Azure service events.
eg: Existing Kafka producers pointing at Azure points to Event Hubs. Reacting to 'a blob was created' with a function points to Event Grid.

term: Cloud design patterns for resilient applications
def: Cache-Aside loads data into a cache on demand. Queue-Based Load Leveling buffers bursts, and Competing Consumers lets several workers drain a queue. Claim Check passes a reference to large payloads instead of the data. Retry handles transient faults, Circuit Breaker stops calls to a failing dependency, and Bulkhead isolates resources so one failure does not spread. CQRS separates reads from writes, Saga manages distributed transactions, and Strangler Fig migrates a system gradually.
eg: A scenario that describes a failure mode is usually asking for the pattern that names it: transient faults, cascading failure, bursts, or oversized messages.

term: Azure API Management tiers and gateways
def: API Management is offered in Consumption (serverless, pay per call), Developer (non-production), Basic, Standard, and Premium tiers, plus the v2 tiers (Basic v2, Standard v2, Premium v2). Network and scale features differ by tier: Premium and Premium v2 support virtual network injection, and Premium supports multi-region deployment. A self-hosted gateway can run in other environments, including on-premises, while being managed from the Azure instance.
eg: Developer has no SLA and is for evaluation. A requirement for a gateway close to on-premises backends points to the self-hosted gateway.

term: Azure Managed Redis and caching design
def: Azure Managed Redis, based on Redis Enterprise, is the in-memory cache and data store to design with, in the Memory Optimized, Balanced, Compute Optimized, and Flash Optimized tiers. Azure Cache for Redis Basic, Standard, and Premium instances retire on September 30, 2028, and the Enterprise and Enterprise Flash tiers on March 31, 2027. Applications usually use the cache-aside pattern, and Azure Front Door, a CDN, and API Management add other caching layers.
eg: A cache is not a system of record. Design for the application to rebuild entries from the database when the cache is empty.

def: Build and release pipelines use GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines, signing in to Azure with workload identity federation (OpenID Connect) instead of stored secrets. Infrastructure is declared in Bicep, ARM templates, or Terraform, and rolled out with deployment slots, Container Apps revisions, or Kubernetes GitOps for blue-green or canary releases. Azure Deployment Environments retires on 22 February 2027, so it is not a basis for new designs.
eg: A pipeline that authenticates with a long-lived secret is the weak point in a design; a federated credential or managed identity is the fix.

def: Azure Migrate is the central hub for discovering servers, databases, and web apps, assessing readiness, right-sizing, and estimating cost, building a business case, analyzing dependencies, and then migrating, using agentless replication for VMware and Hyper-V or an agent-based option for physical servers and other clouds. It integrates with partner tools and with the Database Migration Service.
eg: The assessment results decide which of the migration strategies fits each workload, so assessment comes before any migration tool.

term: Choosing the SQL Server migration target and method
def: SQL Database suits applications that can run without instance-level features. SQL Managed Instance fits near-complete compatibility with SQL Agent and cross-database queries, and can be reached with native backup and restore, the Log Replay Service, or the Managed Instance link for minimal downtime. SQL Server on an Azure VM suits OS-level access or unsupported features. The Database Migration Service runs offline or online migrations to the managed targets.
eg: An assessment first shows which features block the move. Online migration is the answer when the business can tolerate only a short cutover window.

term: Migrating unstructured data: Data Box, Storage Mover, AzCopy
def: Azure Storage Mover is the managed online service for moving files from on-premises or AWS S3 to Azure Storage, with minimal downtime and repeatable jobs. Data Box ships rugged appliances for offline transfer and is suited to data larger than about 40 TB with little or no network capacity; Data Box Disk ships one to five 8-TB SSDs, and Data Box Heavy has been retired. AzCopy is the command-line tool for scripted copies.
eg: Enough bandwidth and an online cutover favor Storage Mover or AzCopy. Tens of terabytes over a slow link favor Data Box.

def: DDoS IP Protection applies per public IP address and DDoS Network Protection applies to a virtual network and the public IPs in it. Network Protection adds DDoS rapid response support, cost protection for scale-out charges during an attack, discounts on Web Application Firewall, and coverage for Basic-tier public IPs. Both tiers use adaptive tuning against the application's traffic profile and integrate with Azure Monitor and Microsoft Sentinel.
eg: A few public IPs without extra services lean to IP Protection. Many IPs in a network, or a need for rapid response and cost protection, lean to Network Protection.

def: A managed service that exchanges routes between network virtual appliances and the Azure network using BGP, so routes are learned and updated dynamically instead of maintaining user-defined routes by hand. It simplifies dynamic routing with SD-WAN and firewall appliances and enables transit between ExpressRoute and VPN gateways.
eg: A requirement for NVAs to advertise routes without hand-edited route tables points to Route Server.

def: A network security perimeter creates a logical boundary around PaaS resources that sit outside your virtual networks, such as Storage accounts, Key Vault, and SQL Database, to control their public network access. Resources are added to a perimeter in Transition (learning, with logging) or Enforced mode, and inbound and outbound rules define what may cross the boundary.
prompt: A _____ creates a logical boundary around PaaS resources that sit outside your virtual networks, such as Storage accounts, Key Vault, and SQL Database, to control their public network access. Resources are added to a perimeter in Transition (learning, with logging) or Enforced mode, and inbound and outbound rules define what may cross the boundary.
eg: Private endpoints bring a PaaS service into a virtual network. A perimeter governs the public path of PaaS-to-PaaS and internet traffic.

def: A central management service for virtual networks at scale: network groups collect virtual networks, connectivity configurations build hub-and-spoke or mesh topologies without peering each pair by hand, and security admin rules apply organization-wide rules that are evaluated before network security group rules.
eg: A central team that must enforce a rule that application teams cannot override with their own NSGs points to security admin rules.

def: Accelerated networking lets a VM's network traffic bypass the host's virtual switch for lower latency and jitter and less CPU use. Proximity placement groups keep related VMs physically close. ExpressRoute FastPath sends data traffic directly to VMs, bypassing the gateway. Front Door and CDN reduce latency to users, and a hub can be placed in the region closest to most traffic.
eg: Latency between tiers in one region points to accelerated networking and proximity placement groups. Latency to far-away users points to Front Door or a CDN.

term: Azure Front Door Standard vs. Premium
def: Both tiers provide global layer-7 routing, caching, TLS offload, and a Web Application Firewall. Premium adds Private Link connections to origins, so that backends such as an internal load balancer or App Service can stay off the public internet, and adds the Microsoft-managed rule set and bot protection that are limited on Standard.
eg: A requirement that origins accept traffic only from Front Door over a private connection points to Premium.
